title: Day 001 — Operational Guide: What Aviation Does
operational_domain: System of Systems, Air Transport, Commerce & Infrastructure
executive_summary: Aviation is far more than a physical flight; it is an interconnected system of international treaties, national sovereignty, commercial investment, ground infrastructure, technical airworthiness, air traffic separation, and human operational control operating across sovereign borders and managed airspace.

kpi_metrics.label: Global Freight Share
kpi_metrics.subtext: Of global freight tonnage transported by air

kpi_metrics.label: Economic Trade Share
kpi_metrics.subtext: Of global trade carried by air by economic value

kpi_metrics.label: Core Stakeholders
kpi_metrics.subtext: Airlines, Aerodromes, ANSPs, MROs, and Ground Handlers

pillars.title: High-Value Global Commerce
pillars.summary: Facilitates just-in-time logistics, carrying high-value pharmaceuticals, electronics, perishables, and emergency spare parts.

pillars.title: Strategic Public Service
pillars.summary: Provides sovereign lifeline connectivity, Public Service Obligations (PSO), emergency search and rescue, and disaster response.

pillars.title: National Economic Integration
pillars.summary: Acts as an economic catalyst driving direct, indirect, and induced jobs across tourism, hospitality, and global manufacturing.

warning_box.title: Systemic Vulnerability Warning
warning_box.description: A flight is never an isolated technical event. Disruption in any single domain—such as ANSP capacity, aerodrome closures, or regulatory non-compliance—cascades rapidly through the global network.

statutory_citations: ICAO Annex 6, Annex 11, Annex 12, and Annex 14
